text.text: The Sharp MZ-2000 was a Japanese home computer released in 1982 as part of Sharp's MZ series. It was an improved version of the earlier MZ-80B, featuring enhanced graphics, more memory, and expansion capabilities. The system used a Z80 processor and included a dedicated display system capable of producing higher-resolution graphics than many competing home computers of the period. Like other Sharp MZ machines, it followed a "clean computer" philosophy where the operating system and programming languages were loaded from external media rather than stored permanently in ROM. The MZ-2000 was primarily used in Japan for programming, education, and hobby computing.
